purpose: P2c-0 golden results of the REAL Lab payout reporter against fake chain/beacon/signer services (HTTP and unix socket only). They prove "same behaviour before and after a refactor", not "same as the real chain and signer".

crossCheck.result: 16 of 17 scenarios identical (state digests, signer requests, per-event-key payment counts, key log lines); only s02_invariant_c_on differs: df78e6b has no invariant C and pays all five pending entries in one batch, P1 holds the ones ahead of the committed cursor (two batches 4+1) - the known P1 change

normalization: see labE2e/harness.test.ts header: ANSI and logger prefix removed; ISO timestamps, durations and the wall-clock scalars updatedAt/createdAt/gasWaitStartedAt/frozenAt become placeholders; generation names and manifest writtenAt dropped; nothing else is relaxed
determinism: recorded once, then compared on the P1 root 2 x 5 concurrent runs (heavy CPU load), once alone, and on the P2 checkout: identical; the first comparison exposed freezeH.frozenAt (wall clock, normalized); load exposed an ethers-internal extra eth_blockNumber that broke a head plan counted per RPC call, so the head is now driven per tick over HTTP (/e2e/tick)
review: independent review of efbc3fd: F1 per-event-key payment counts (asserted <= 1 in every scenario), F2 stray output must be empty, F3 only the reporter tick scheduler timer is shortened (delay 15000 and stack contains scheduleNextLabTick), F4 the group runs by default; scenario s17 added; review G1 negative control and non-empty event keys (labE2eHarness.test.ts), G2 in-flight reader for version 2 and WAL/version 3 states, G3 the harness fails when the child timed out or finished without compressing any tick timer (the child prints compressed=N requested=T; fixtures re-recorded: only that line was added)
